headline: Watch: Hormuz shipping attacks and uncertain US-Iran talks keep fuel risk the main concern, with no confirmed impacts on Australia.
summary: Little change overnight. Ships are still being struck near Hormuz and US-Iran talks are uncertain, but oil fell about 5% to US$93.50 and markets calmed. The collector's pandemic warning was checked and is not confirmed: the main real item is the Ebola outbreak in Africa, which is distant. All Australian phone and internet networks are normal and there are no SA weather emergencies.
actions: Keep the car tank and any generator fuel at least half full while Hormuz shipping remains disrupted.

categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict

sources.title: Status of US-Iran talks uncertain as ship struck in Hormuz (Reuters wrap)
Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan 'unconvincing'; Trump confirms strikes (Al Jazeera)
Oil falls as Trump signals restraint on Iran (TimesLIVE, 9 Nov)

categories.summary: The US-Iran conflict continues: Hormuz shipping attacks persist and US-Iran talks are uncertain after US strikes on Iranian targets on 3 Nov. Taiwan sees routine Chinese military activity only; no new direct threat to Australia found.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: No nuclear-command aircraft airborne and no nuclear alert signs. Iran's nuclear programme remains part of stalled negotiations.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: No Australian carrier outages (all networks normal). Routine breaches reported (a healthcare provider ransomware attack, an SA oral health scheme data breach) but nothing large-scale. Global threat level green; ACSC feed timed out again.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological

sources.title: WHO Disease Outbreak News: Bundibugyo virus disease (6 Nov)
Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 in DR Congo (Al Jazeera)

categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has passed 10,000 cases with imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria. Serious but distant; risk to SA is limited to rare imported cases. The collector's other pandemic signs were false positives.

categories.name: Natural hazards

sources.title: USGS M6.4 – 30 km WSW of Lata, Solomon Islands

categories.summary: No GDACS orange/red alerts. The M6.4 Solomon Islands quake produced no tsunami. No current SA severe weather or bushfire emergencies found.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply

sources.title: Oil falls as Trump says fresh Iran attacks unlikely (Reuters via Investing.com)

categories.summary: Hormuz disruption keeps fuel supply tight after this year's shortages and refinery fire, but oil fell about 5% and no current shortage or rationing was found.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Brent down 4.9% to about US$93.50, VIX down 21% to 20.3, gold US$4,115, AUD 0.692. Markets calmer than recent days.

concerns.title: Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping
drivers: Ships are still being struck near Hormuz and US-Iran talks are uncertain after US strikes on Iranian targets on 3 Nov.
Oil eased on signals of US restraint.
Australia imports most of its fuel, so this is the main path to SA.

scenarios.name: Talks drag on, sporadic attacks continue
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices stay high and volatile; occasional regional servo shortages but no rationing.

scenarios.name: Deal reached, shipping recovers
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices ease over weeks; little direct effect on SA.

scenarios.name: Major escalation or full Hormuz closure
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel price jump and local shortages within 1-3 weeks; possible government fuel measures.

actions.action: Keep the car and any generator fuel at least half full.
actions.reason: In an escalation, stations run dry within days from panic buying; a half tank covers about a week of essential trips.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

concerns.title: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak (Africa)
drivers: WHO reports over 10,000 cases and a ~49% fatality rate in DR Congo, with imported cases in Kenya and Nigeria.
The collector's 'mystery pneumonia' and chemical matches were old or unrelated stories.

scenarios.name: Outbreak stays in Africa
scenarios.sa_impact: No direct effect; possible extra airport screening.

scenarios.name: Isolated imported case in a Western country
scenarios.sa_impact: Media concern; Australian hospitals manage under existing plans.

scenarios.name: Spread in Asia-Pacific
scenarios.sa_impact: Travel restrictions and health system alerts.

actions.action: Check Smartraveller before any travel to Central or East Africa.
actions.reason: Advice and entry rules can change quickly as the outbreak spreads.

concerns.title: Taiwan Strait pressure
drivers: Taiwan reports routine daily Chinese aircraft and ship activity; no live-fire warnings, GPS jamming or blockade signs.
A Chinese state-hacking report lit one indicator but is background.

scenarios.name: Blockade or quarantine
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel, medicine and electronics disruption within weeks.

actions.action: Keep 2-3 months of any essential prescription medicines.
actions.reason: Most medicines are imported via Asian shipping lanes, which any blockade would disrupt first.

concerns.title: Russia-NATO tensions
drivers: Reports of Russians leaving amid new draft fears; no NATO-Russia incident found.
Baltic GPS jamming is at its usual high level (18%); the US has a departure order for Belarus (long-standing).

scenarios.name: Wider mobilisation or NATO incident
scenarios.sa_impact: Market shock, higher fuel prices and more cyber attacks globally.

scenarios.name: Direct Russia-NATO conflict
scenarios.sa_impact: Severe global market and energy shock.

actions.action: Keep devices and banking apps updated
actions.reason: Russian-linked cyber campaigns spill over to Australian businesses and households during tense periods.

concerns.title: Cyber attacks on Australian services
drivers: Several Australian data breaches reported (healthcare ransomware, an SA oral-health scheme breach), but no attack on telcos, banks or the grid.
All carrier networks are normal and the global threat level is green.

scenarios.name: Hours-long outage of payments or a telco
scenarios.sa_impact: Card payments and phones down for hours.

scenarios.name: Multi-day multi-sector attack
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, fuel and communications disrupted for days.

actions.reason: Card payments and EFTPOS stop during telco or bank outages, which is the most likely cyber impact.

concerns.title: AI-enabled attack (non-traditional)
drivers: New reports of AI-enabled tools used against banks and to steal Taipei emergency records, plus fake nuclear warnings sent via Russian and Ukrainian alert systems (reported, not verified).
No deepfake of Australian officials or mass AI-driven attack on Australia found.

scenarios.name: Background AI-assisted crime and espionage
scenarios.sa_impact: More convincing scams and data breaches; no wide outage.

scenarios.name: Synthetic-media crisis (fake leader video or alert)
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of confusion, possible panic buying before it is debunked.

scenarios.name: Machine-speed attack on many systems at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, telcos, hospitals or the grid disrupted for hours to days.

actions.action: Agree a family code word for urgent calls
actions.reason: AI can clone a voice from seconds of audio; a code word defeats fake 'I need help now' calls.

actions.action: Check shocking videos or alerts against official channels before acting
actions.reason: Fakes are designed to make people act fast; ABC radio and alert.sa.gov.au confirm what is real.

events_observed.title: US strikes on Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz
